S97P: Akal Purakh is One, whose name is 'the One who exists', who is the creator of the creation, who pervades all, who is free of fear, who is free of enmity, whose form is beyond time (that is, whose body is free of destruction), who does not come into the cycle of births, whose light has come from himself, and who is found by the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. Truth Is The Name. Creative Being Personified. No Fear. No Hatred. Image Of The Undying. Beyond Birth. Self-Existent. By Guru's Grace:
There is but one God. True is His Name, creative His personality and Immortal His form. he is without fear, sans enmity, unborn and self-illumined and is obtained by the Guru's grace.
7GV5: Raag Bilaval, in Ghar 1, the four-stanza bani of Guru Nanak Dev ji.
Raag Bilaaval, First Mehl, Chau-Padhay, First House:
9J4Q: Kaha hau = I say. Kavan vadaee = there is no greatness.
O Lord! By praising you I am not doing you any greatness; (it is just as though) you are an emperor and I am calling you a mian.
You are the Emperor, and I call You a chief - how does this add to Your greatness?
You are a sovereign, How is it to Your greatness?

O Waheguru! You who are the emperor of all — and if I utter the word "mian" for you, then what greatness of yours is that? He gives an illustration: just as calling some great emperor "mian" brings him no greatness, and hearing it he is not pleased either, so too, O Nirankar! By saying Ravanari, Madhsudan, Murari and the rest there is no complete greatness of yours — that is, you are of an unmade and imperishable form; or, (kaha) where are you (sultan) the emperor and where am I (mia) a petty chief, the meaning being that you are Ishvar and I a trifling creature. Who am I, that I might tell your boundless greatness?
SG63: (But even this much praising is not within my own power) O master-Lord! However much strength (for praising) you give, that much of your qualities do I utter. Your qualities cannot be described by me, the ignorant one. ||1||
As You permit me, I praise You, O Lord and Master; I am ignorant, and I cannot chant Your Praises. ||1||
As you inspire me, so do I praise You, O Lord, Myself, I am ignorant and can say not Yours praises.
Therefore, O master! Whatever speech you give, that do I utter. Without your grace, your greatness cannot be told at any length by me, the fool. ||1||
00KD: Gava = may I sing. Bujhaee = understanding, wisdom.
O Lord! Grant me such understanding that I may be able to sing your praise.
Please bless me with such understanding, that I may sing Your Glorious Praises.
Bless You me with understanding to sing Yours excellences,
O Waheguru! Give such understanding to me, by which I may sing your qualities.
Z2P7: Jaise = in such a way, so that. Rahau = may I remain fixed. Rajaee = O Lord, master of the will! ||1|| Rahau ||
O Lord, master of the will! You are the one who abides for ever, and by the grace of your praise may I remain fixed at your (feet). ||1|| Rahau ||
May I dwell in Truth, according to Your Will. ||1||Pause||
so that I may abide in Truth, according to Your will, O Lord. Pause.

Again, O (rajaee) emperor who gives the command! Show such grace that I may remain established for ever in your form of truth. If you should say, "and what then? You are already singing my qualities." ||1|| Rahau || To that he says:
WZXQ: Tujh te = from you. Asnaee = naee, greatness {'sna' is an Arabic word, its meaning is 'greatness'}. {Note: when at the beginning of a word there are two joined letters of which the first is 's', then in Punjabi pronunciation those two letters are separated and an 'a' is used before the 's'. Or, the 's' is dropped altogether; for example: (स्थान) satan = asthan, than. (स्तम्भ) stambh = asthambh, thambh, thamh. (स्टेशन) stashan = astashan, teshan. (स्ना) sna = asnaee, naee (an Arabic word)}.
However much of this world has come to be, all of it has come to be from you alone; all this is your own greatness.
Whatever has happened, has all come from You. You are All-knowing.
Whatever has happened, all that has come from You. You has friendship with all.
Whatever all this expanse has come to be, all of it has come to be from your thought alone; and again, your (asnaee) love is within all.
HF90: Sahib = O Sahib! Chaturaee = wisdom, cleverness. ||2||
O master-Lord! I cannot know the limit of your qualities. I am blind (I am of trifling understanding); there is no such wisdom in me (that I might know the limit of your qualities). ||2||
Your limits cannot be known, O my Lord and Master; I am blind - what wisdom do I have? ||2||
I know not your limit, O my Lord. What wisdom have I, a blind man?

O my Sahib! I do not know your limit. There is no cleverness of mine, the blind one — the meaning being that it is by your grace alone that your form can be known. The meaning being that whatever I have said before, all of it has been said by your grace alone. ||2||
NTR8: Hau = I. Kathi = may I describe. Kathe kath = kath kath, having told and told. Dekha = I see. Akath = the one whose qualities cannot be told.
I cannot tell your qualities at all. When I look, having uttered and uttered your qualities (then I come to understand that) your form is beyond description, and I am not fit to describe it.
What should I say? While talking, I talk of seeing, but I cannot describe the indescribable.
What should I say? While talking of You I see that I cannot describe the Indescribable Lord.

(Kathi) those shastras which have been uttered by the utterers of your praise — what shall I utter of them and see? Or, becoming an utterer, I have uttered your discourse and seen. O (akath) Waheguru! Your entire praise cannot be uttered by me.
WBET: Even the least little of your greatness that I utter, I utter only that which is pleasing to you (that is, as much as you yourself give the understanding to describe). ||3||
As it pleases Your Will, I speak; it is just the tiniest bit of Your greatness. ||3||
Whatever pleases You, that alone speak I and that is but an iota of your greatness.
For that reason, O Kartar! Whatever is pleasing to you, that alone, (til) in a little measure, do I utter of your greatness. ||3||
URWL: Ete = so many, countless. Kookar = dogs, the vices such as lust. Begana = a stranger. Bhauka = I bark. Is tan taee = for the saving of this body.

(O Lord! Here) there are countless dogs (of lust and the rest), and I am a stranger (fallen among them); (whatever praise of you I make, that too) I bark only for the saving of this body of mine (from the dogs of lust and the rest, just as a stranger dog barks to save itself from hostile dogs).
Among so many dogs, I am an outcast; I bark for my body's belly.
Among so many dogs, I am a stranger dog and bark for this body's belly of mine.

O Waheguru! If I make (ete koo) this pride (begana) a stranger — that is, if I forsake it. What pride? That I say I do even a little of your greatness — then what fear is there to this body, that is, to the mind indicated by the subtle body? The meaning being that it will assuredly become fearless. Or, (ete) those such as Byas who (kookar) call out, that is, utter, your praise — and if (hau) I too sing, then what fear is there to this body of mine?
RHWG: Khasmai nau = the Name of the master, the greatness of the master, the majesty of the master. Na jaee = cannot be removed. ||4||1||

(I have this assurance, that) if (your servant) Nanak is empty of devotion (even then you are the protecting master over my head, and) this glory of the master has not been removed from you (that from time out of mind you have gone on helping the one who comes to your refuge). ||4||1||
Without devotional worship, O Nanak, even so, still, my Master's Name does not leave me. ||4||1||
Though Nanak be bereft of Lord's meditation, even then he sill bear the Name of his Master.

Even if I be without devotion, still I am your own servant, and you are my master. This name will never go away — the meaning being that you yourself, keeping the honour of your servants, will make them one with your own form. ||4||1|| ☬ Again he makes a supplication face to face:
CDQQ: Mandar = the abode of the deity. Tan = the body (that is, the organs of perception). Ves kalandar = one in the garb of a faqir. Kalandar = a faqir, a wandering faqir. Ghat hee = ghat hee, within the heart itself. Teerath = upon the place of pilgrimage. Nava = I bathe.

My mind has become the temple (for the Lord-deity to dwell in), my body (that is, each of my organs of perception, which makes the pilgrimage to the temple) has become a wandering sadhu (that is, my organs of perception, instead of wandering outside, have turned towards the Lord dwelling within); now I bathe at the pilgrimage-place of the heart itself.
My mind is the temple, and my body is the simple cloth of the humble seeker; deep within my heart, I bathe at the sacred shrine.
My body is clothed with the mendicant's dress, my mind is the temple and I bathe in my heart's pilgrim's place.

O Hari! To bring under control the monkey that is the mind, I have taken upon my body the (kalandar) garb of the detached faqirs. Or, within the temple of the body I have made the mind — that is, I have turned it inward. This very thing is the (kalandar) garb of the saint; and those saints of the kalandari garb who go upon the pilgrimage of the holy places — here, within the vessel that is the inner self, that certainty of your form which is to be made, in that very holy place of pilgrimage do I bathe. Or, within the mind are the garbs of the body, and the strife and affliction too are within the mind; if I bring this mind under control, then within (ghar) the body itself I shall bathe in the holy place of the self — the meaning being that I shall become one who is blissful in the self.
U16H: Ek sabad = the shabad of the Lord's praise. Merai pran = within my soul. Janam = in birth. Bahur = again, once more. Ava = I shall come. ||1||
The shabad of the Lord's praise has become fixed within my soul (it has become the support of my soul. For this reason I have become certain that) I shall not come into birth again. ||1||
The One Word of the Shabad abides within my mind; I shall not come to be born again. ||1||
The One Lord's Name abides in my mind and I shall not be born again.

O (ek) unequalled (sabad) Brahm! You who are the support of my life-breaths — that is, my very life — dwell for ever within my heart, and therefore, becoming absorbed within your form, I shall not come again into birth and death. ||1||
C6Y0: Bedhia = has been pierced. Seti = with. Meri maee = O my mother!
O my mother! (My) mind has been pierced through in (the feet of) the Lord, the home of mercy.
My mind is pierced through by the Merciful Lord, O my mother!
My soul is pierced by the Merciful Master, O my mother.
O (maee) Waheguru, lord of Maya, merciful to the lowly! Such love has arisen in me for your feet that my mind, meeting with your form, has become (bedhia) one with it.
DEQ8: Kaun janai = no one else knows. Peer = pain.
I have become certain that (apart from the Lord) no other can understand another's pain and sorrow.
Who can know the pain of another?
Who knows the pain of another?
Now who can know the sorrows of (paraee) relations and the rest?
AE92: Chint paraee = the hope of any other. ||1|| Rahau ||
Now I keep no hope of any other (apart from the Lord). ||1|| Rahau ||
I think of none other than the Lord. ||1||Pause||
Without the Lord, I think not of another. Pause.
Because for us there is no care of any other at all. ||1|| Rahau ||
1AG7: Agam = O unapproachable one! Agocharu = a-go-char, the one whom the senses cannot reach. Alakh = invisible. Chinta = care, attention, keeping. Karahu = you do.
O unapproachable one! O one beyond the senses! O invisible one! O boundless Lord! It is you alone who take care of all of us beings.
O Lord, inaccessible, unfathomable, invisible and infinite: please, take care of me!
O my Inaccessible, Incomprehensible, Invisible and Infinite Lord, take care of me.

Therefore, O Waheguru who are (agam) beyond the mind, (agochar) beyond the eyes and beyond speech, invisible and of boundless form! It is you alone who take all the care of feeding and sustaining us and the rest of the creatures.
HUGU: Maheeal = mahee tal, upon the surface of the earth, in the open space, in the sky. Bharipur = brimful, filled to the brim. Ghat = in the heart. Ghat ghat = in each and every heart. ||2||
You are pervading, filled to the brim, everywhere — in the water, in the earth, in the sky; within the heart of each and every (being) your light is present. ||2||
In the water, on the land and in sky, You are totally pervading. Your Light is in each and every heart. ||2||
You are completely contained in sea, land, lower and upper regions and in every heart is yours light.

Outwardly you are contained, brimful, in the waters, the lands, (mahee) the earth and (al) the sky, in the whole universe; and within, in each and every heart, it is your (jot) conscious being alone that is shining. ||2||
G59M: Sikh = instruction. Mat = wisdom. Mandir = the minds (as temples) of beings. Chhava = the body.
O my master-Lord! The minds and bodies of all beings are fashioned by you alone; instruction, wisdom and understanding come to all beings from you alone.
All teachings, instructions and understandings are Yours; the mansions and sanctuaries are Yours as well.
My instruction and understanding are all Yours. My mansions and sanctuaries belong to You.

(Sikh) the shastra, (mat) the wisdom of conduct, and the intellect that dwells upon the self — all this is given by you alone. O my Waheguru who are (mandir) the form of my support! Within your form I ever (chhava) establish my mind.
2HT7: Jana = I know. Gava = I sing. ||3||
I know no other as your equal. I ever sing your qualities alone. ||3||
Without You, I know no other, O my Lord and Master; I continually sing Your Glorious Praises. ||3||
Without You, O my Lord, I know not any other. I ever sing Yours praises.
Therefore, O my Sahib! Apart from you I know no other, and therefore I ever sing your qualities alone. ||3||
KAUC: Sabh = all. Chint = care, keeping. Tudh pase = with you, to you alone.
All beings and creatures have your support alone; to you alone belongs the care of keeping them all.
All beings and creatures seek the Protection of Your Sanctuary; all thought of their care rests with You.
Men and other beings all seek Your protection, All anxiety for them rests with You.
These creatures, (jant) the subtle and gross beings, are all come into your refuge, and the care of sustaining them all is with you alone — that is, you alone are the sustainer of all.
QLT4: Nanak's only supplication (at your door) is this, that whatever your will may be, may it be pleasing to me (may I ever remain content in your will). ||4||2||
That which pleases Your Will is good; this alone is Nanak's prayer. ||4||2||
Whatever pleases You, O Lord that is good. this alone is Nanak's supplication.

Sri Guru ji says: O Akal Purakh! Whatever is pleasing to you, that alone may I know as good within my heart; this one thing alone is my (ardase) supplication before you. ||4||2|| ☬ Showing Waheguru to be the form of all, he makes his supplication:
